title: Tell the caller what the host's answer asks for

blocks.text: This picks up where the previous practice ended. The file already contains its solution.

The client now reads the host's answers with the network's own code list, which its constructor receives as a map from field 39 codes to a `Category`. The network's operations team sent a list of complaints:

items: Some cardholders were told "declined" and were charged anyway.
On the night the issuer was down for maintenance, some cardholders were told their card was declined, and others were charged twice.
After Tuesday's release the host rejected every purchase from one terminal model for six hours. Each cardholder was told "declined", and nobody on the team found out.

During a host upgrade, some answers came back with no field 39, and some with a code that isn't on the network's list. The client reported them all as declines. The host's records show that some were approvals.

blocks.text: Finish `outcomeOf` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PaymentClient.java`. The `Outcome` enum has a value for every kind of ending. Anything the developers must look at goes onto the `alerts` queue of the space (`sp.out`), and `unknown(...)` hands a message to the reversal process. About ten lines.

cases.says: an answer the network lists as an approval or a decline is reported as such, with nothing left to reverse
every code the network lists as an approval moved the money, not only 00
an unavailable issuer or switch means the cardholder may try later, not that the card was declined
trying later is a new transaction, so the same message is not sent again
a format error says the request is wrong, so it raises an alert instead of passing as a decline
an answer without field 39 decides nothing, so it is treated like no answer and reversed
a code the network's list doesn't contain decides nothing either, and is reversed rather than called a decline

concepts: Field 39 is read from the network's list: approvals other than 00, try later as a new transaction, format errors as the developers' problem.
An answer with no field 39 or with a code not on the list decides nothing, and is treated like no answer and reversed.
